transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish reviewing claims. It’s becoming a problem at work.
What feeling or sensation makes you want to get up from your desk?
I just feel like I need to get up and step away from the workstation, even though I know I should stay and finish reviewing the claims.
Do you feel an uncomfortable or restless sensation in your legs that drives this urge to get up?
No, I haven’t noticed anything uncomfortable or restless in my legs. It’s more just that I feel like I need to step away from the desk.
What thoughts or feelings are going through your mind right before you decide to get up?

Right before I get up, I’m usually thinking that I need to step away for a minute. Even though I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish the claim reviews, I just end up getting up from the workstation.
Did you have trouble sitting still or paying attention like this when you were a child?
Yeah, looking back, it wasn’t new. In elementary school, my teachers would say I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets, miss instructions, and need reminders to finish my classwork.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting with your hands or feet, or tapping them, while seated?
Yeah. In longer trainings or team meetings, I’m usually bouncing my leg, clicking a pen, or shifting around in my chair, even when I’m trying to look focused.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others while they are talking?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself cutting people off a lot, at least not deliberately.
Do you often feel 'on the go,' as if you're driven by a motor?
I’m not sure I’d describe myself that way. What do you mean by “driven by a motor”?
Do you often find yourself talking excessively, or feel like you talk much more than others?
I don’t think I talk more than other people, at least not that I’ve noticed. I’m usually pretty aware of giving other people a chance to speak.
Do you often have a hard time waiting your turn, like when standing in line or waiting for your turn in group situations?
I don’t think so. Waiting in line or taking turns usually isn’t something I’ve noticed being especially hard for me.
Do you often make careless mistakes or overlook important details when working on your claim reviews?
I’m not really sure. I try to look things over carefully, so I haven’t noticed a pattern of making careless mistakes.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things happening around you or by your own thoughts when you are trying to work?

Yeah. If people nearby start talking about another claim, or I suddenly remember some random errand, my attention just kind of slides off what I’m reading. Then I have to go back and reread the same section a few times.
Do you often have difficulty organizing your tasks or managing your time to get work done?

Yeah, especially since my caseload got bigger. My claim folders, notes, and email flags end up kind of all over the place, and I have trouble figuring out which policy review I should start with first.

These symptoms began in elementary school (prior to age 12) and result in clear occupational impairment, meeting criteria for ICD-10 F90.0 (Disturbance of activity and attention / ADHD).
